problem.name: Gibbs sampling
problem.statement_latex:
Given $H:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $\beta$, generate a sample within total-variation error $\varepsilon$ of $\pi_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta H(x)}/Z(\beta)$. For an integer-valued objective with unit gap, choosing $\beta\ge\log(|\Omega|/\eta)$ makes an optimum occur with probability at least $1-\eta$. Thus sampling can yield discrete optimization.
The chain-based comparison counts coherent or classical transition steps; explicit constraint-model sampling also has a classical bit-time bound.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(L/\sqrt\delta)$ coherent walk steps, quantum simulated annealing and quantum sampling.
quantum.details_latex: The theorem assumes a supplied sequence of $L$ reversible chains with gap at least $\delta$, an efficiently prepared initial distribution and suitable overlap between adjacent stationary states. Accuracy and overlap parameters contribute logarithmic or explicit factors. Measuring the final coherent Gibbs state produces a sample.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(L/\sqrt\delta)$ coherent walk steps, quantum simulated annealing and quantum sampling.
quantum.details_text: The theorem assumes a supplied sequence of $L$ reversible chains with gap at least $\delta$, an efficiently prepared initial distribution and suitable overlap between adjacent stationary states. Accuracy and overlap parameters contribute logarithmic or explicit factors. Measuring the final coherent Gibbs state produces a sample.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(L/\delta)$ transition steps, sequential classical mixing; subexponential conditional counting for sparse explicit models.
classical.details_latex: Warm starts and the smallest relevant stationary probability enter the mixing bound. Sparse fixed-width hard constraints admit exact uniform sampling in expected $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time by conditional counts. For sparse constant-arity, constant-bit integer energies, conditional counts at the $O(n)$ possible energies yield Gibbs samples to total-variation error $\varepsilon$ with the same exponent and polynomial numerical overhead. The smaller applicable sampler determines the explicit-instance comparison.

strength.description_latex: Quadratic improvement in inverse spectral gap for the specified chain sequence, from quantum-walk phase detection and state transformations. An exponentially small gap gives an improvement in the exponential constant of that chain-based bound.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous relative-to-chain algorithmic speedup. Explicit-instance comparisons also include samplers obtained from counting.

hardware.description_latex: A configuration requires $\log_2|\Omega|$ logical data qubits plus reversible transition, energy and phase-estimation workspace. Fault-tolerant depth scales with $L/\sqrt\delta$ and can remain exponential for slowly mixing chains.
